Chapter 1. Compactness

1.1. Open Covers

This section establishes the Heine-Borel property and its consequences. Textbooks frequently interpose a remark between a theorem and its proof; this fixture exercises that structure to confirm the chunker does not falsely pair across the intervening remark.

Theorem 1.1 (Heine-Borel).

A subset of ℝn is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

Remark 1.2.

The forward direction fails in infinite-dimensional normed spaces, where closed bounded sets need not be compact.

Proof.

Reduce to the case of a closed box via boundedness, then apply the finite-subcover argument to a bisection sequence. The converse follows from continuity of the coordinate projections.
